advanceOrder and cancelOrder hand state changes to the domain through order.advanceTo(target) and order.cancel().
The loop that checks products[index].stock < items[index].quantity before reserving makes the order all-or-nothing across several products, which is coordination work.

parsedVerdict.reasoning:
OrderService behaves like a normal application-layer use-case service. It loads aggregates through domain repository interfaces, coordinates operations across aggregates (it reserves product stock and creates an Order, and it cancels an order and releases its stock), saves through those repository ports, and maps entities to DTOs. The file has no persistence code (no SQL, storage or ORM), no transport code (no HTTP, request or response handling) and no framework code.

Order state changes are handed to the domain through order.advanceTo and order.cancel. Stock changes are handed to the domain through product.reserve and product.release.

Two parts are borderline but still fit the application role:
- The stock check before any reservation (products[index].stock < items[index].quantity) is cross-aggregate coordination. It makes the order all-or-nothing, so no stock is changed unless every item can be reserved. This is not a core domain rule moved out of the domain.
- combineItems validates the incoming DTO shape and merges duplicate product lines. That is input normalisation, which belongs in the application layer. Its "at least one item" check could also be enforced inside Order, but having it here does not move a responsibility to the wrong layer kind.

The in-memory nextId counter is a weak ID-generation choice, but it is not infrastructure logic as the rubric means it.
